practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient/Mongoose connection (singleton) and tune pool options for your deployment scenario rather than creating new clients per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a connection pool and sensible driver options: set maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, and enable retryWrites where supported; reuse one shared Mongoose/driver connection across the app and close it on shutdown.

practices.practice: Persist change-stream resume tokens durably (e.g., in a small collection or durable store) so streams can be resumed after restarts or transient errors.
practices.prior_belief: Persist and use change stream resume tokens so the monitor can recover from restarts and transient errors without losing events; store the resume token outside memory (e.g., a small collection or durable store) after every processed event batch.

practices.practice: Keep heartbeat documents small and split or store large attachments outside the database (for example, Azure Blob Storage) to avoid reaching the 16 MB BSON document limit and to reduce RU spikes.
practices.prior_belief: Keep heartbeat documents small and fixed-shape (e.g., {atmId, status, cashLevel, ts, geo}) and store large attachments or logs off-db (blob storage) to avoid large-document limits and RU spikes.

practices.practice: Create indexes that match read/query patterns—use a compound index following the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range) such as { atmId: 1, timestamp: -1 } for latest-heartbeat queries and a single-field index on status for fast aggregations.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that match read/query patterns: at minimum index atmId and ts (compound index {atmId:1, ts:-1}) for latest-heartbeat queries and index status for fast availability aggregation.

practices.practice: Maintain a single network summary document per scope and update it with atomic single-document operations (upsert / $inc / $set) rather than recomputing the whole summary on every change to reduce RU cost and race windows.
practices.prior_belief: Maintain a single network summary document per monitored scope and update it atomically with update operators (e.g., updateOne with $inc, $set) or upsert, rather than recomputing from scratch on every change to reduce RU costs and race conditions.

practices.practice: Avoid multi-document or cross-partition transactions for high-throughput heartbeat ingestion; prefer single-document atomic updates or idempotent upserts and only use transactions when necessary and within documented limits.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions for high-throughput heartbeat writes; prefer single-document atomic updates or idempotent upserts for summary/alert state to minimize cross-partition transactions and RU consumption.

practices.practice: Use a TTL index on a Date field to expire old heartbeat documents (or run a controlled background prune job) and understand TTL semantics (date field required, ~60s sweeper granularity, single-field only).
practices.prior_belief: Use a TTL mechanism to expire old heartbeat documents to control storage growth (e.g., TTL index on ts) or implement a background prune job if TTL indexes are not available/compatible with the engine.

practices.practice: Monitor request-unit (RU) consumption and index usage and provision sufficient throughput or enable autoscale to handle ingestion spikes from many frequent heartbeats.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor RU/s (or request units) and index usage; provision sufficient throughput or enable autoscale to handle ingestion spikes from many ATMs sending frequent heartbeats.

practices.practice: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for client retries on transient network/429/5xx errors and leverage driver-level retry settings where supported, limiting attempts to avoid thundering retries.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff and jitter for transient network/429/5xx errors and integrate driver-level retryWrites when available; limit retry attempts to avoid overwhelming the server.

practices.practice: When using change streams, apply a server-side aggregation pipeline ($match) to filter events you don't need so you reduce event volume and associated costs.
practices.prior_belief: When using change streams, filter server-side with an aggregate pipeline ($match on fullDocument.atmId or status) to reduce event volume and RU/throughput costs.

practices.practice: Persist alert state (active alerts, lastTriggeredAt) in the database and make alert writes idempotent or deduplicated (use uniqueness constraints or transactional patterns) to avoid duplicate notifications from flapping events.
practices.prior_belief: Persist alert state (e.g., active alerts list, lastTriggeredAt) in the DB and de-duplicate alert notifications by using idempotent writes/conditional updates so transient flapping doesn't cause repeated alerts.

practices.practice: Prefer explicit, documented guidance for readPreference/readConcern only when the service documents their mapping for the MongoDB driver; do not assume MongoDB defaults map identically without checking Azure DocumentDB compatibility docs.
practices.prior_belief: Use appropriate readPreference/readConcern for your consistency needs (e.g., majority/primary for correctness of status and summaries) but be aware of compatibility/latency tradeoffs on the managed service.

practices.practice: Model per-ATM current state in a dedicated collection with a unique index on atmId for cheap lookups and fast updates rather than scanning heartbeat history.
practices.prior_belief: Model per-ATM state in a dedicated collection with a unique index on atmId to allow cheap lookups and fast updates for online/offline checks rather than scanning heartbeat history.

practices.practice: When using Mongoose, declare strict schemas, explicit indexes, and avoid heavy middleware on the hot insert path; rely on lightweight validation and explicit indexes for performance-sensitive workloads.
practices.prior_belief: When building Mongoose schemas, set strict schemas, appropriate field types, and explicit indexes in the schema, and avoid Mongoose middleware that blocks high-throughput insert paths (prefer lightweight validation or pre-validation off the hot path).
